questions.prompt: The sublevel set of a function \(f\) at height \(a\) is
questions.explanation: The sublevel set \(\mathrm{lev}(f, a)\) keeps every point whose value is less than or equal to \(a\). Equality alone is the contour set. The opposite inequality is a superlevel set. The domain is where \(f\) is defined, not where it is small.

questions.prompt: The sublevel set of \(f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2\) at height 16 is a closed disk. What is its radius?
questions.explanation: The inequality \(x^2 + y^2 \le 16\) is the closed disk of radius \(\sqrt{16} = 4\). The contour at the same height is the circle of that radius, not a disk of radius 16. The diameter would be 8. The height 16 is the squared radius, not the radius.

questions.prompt: The contour set of \(f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2\) at height 16 is
questions.explanation: A contour set is the equality \(x^2 + y^2 = 16\), a circle of radius 4. The disk, interior included, is the sublevel set at that height. The origin has value 0, so it lies in the sublevel set and not on this contour. A round level set of this \(f\) is not a line.

options: the disk of radius 4, including the interior

questions.prompt: Let \(a > 0\) and \(c > 0\). The sublevel set \(\{t \in \mathbb{R} : c t^2 \le a\}\) is a closed interval. Write its right endpoint as an expression in the names a and c.
questions.explanation:
The inequality \(c t^2 \le a\) rearranges, for \(c > 0\), to \(t^2 \le a/c\). The right endpoint is the positive square root \(\sqrt{a/c}\).
• \(a/c\) is the square of that endpoint.
• \(\sqrt{a} - \sqrt{c}\) subtracts lengths that are not the two sides of this inequality.
• \(c/a\) inverts the ratio. The function value grows when \(c\) grows, so the sublevel set shrinks.

questions.prompt: On the contour \(x^2 + 4 y^2 = 16\), what is the largest value of \(y\)?
questions.explanation: The largest \(y\) occurs where \(x = 0\), so \(4 y^2 = 16\), \(y^2 = 4\), and the positive solution is 2. The positive \(x\)-intercept is 4, which solves \(x^2 = 16\). The height 16 is not a coordinate. The semi-axis in \(y\) is the number asked for.

questions.prompt: Put these steps in order to sketch the sublevel set of \(f(x, y) = (x/3)^2 + (y/2)^2\) at height 1.
questions.explanation: The equality case is the contour, an ellipse with semi-axes 3 and 2, and that curve is the boundary. A test point decides which side belongs to the sublevel set: the origin has value 0, which is below 1, so the inside is the side to shade. The inequality is \(\le\), so the boundary is included. Shading before the test point can fill the outside. Dropping the boundary would draw a strict sublevel set.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 280 210" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>shaded elliptical disk</title><line x1="28" y1="108" x2="256" y2="108"/><polygon points="256,108 249.6,110.7 249.6,105.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="140" y1="186" x2="140" y2="24"/><polygon points="140,24 142.7,30.4 137.3,30.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="250" y="124" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">x1</text><text x="148" y="28" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">x2</text><ellipse cx="140" cy="108" rx="88" ry="48" fill="currentColor" fill-opacity="0.12"/></svg>
questions.figure_alt: A shaded ellipse, longer along the first axis.
steps: Read the equality \(f(x, y) = 1\) as an ellipse and record its semi-axes.
Draw that ellipse. It is the boundary of the sublevel set.
Evaluate \(f\) at the origin and compare the value with 1.
Shade the inside of the ellipse, including the boundary, because the inequality is not strict.

questions.prompt: For \(f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2\), which of these points lie in the sublevel set at height 4?
questions.explanation: The values are 0, 4, 10, and 2. The sublevel set keeps values at most 4, so the origin, \((2, 0)\), and \((1, -1)\) belong. The point \((2, 0)\) is on the contour, and a non-strict sublevel set includes its contour. The point \((3, 1)\) has value 10 and is outside. Leaving out the origin would confuse the sublevel set with the contour.

questions.prompt: On the contour \(2x + y = 10\), what is \(y\) when \(x = 3\)?
questions.explanation: Substitute \(x = 3\): \(6 + y = 10\), so \(y = 4\). The contour of a linear function is a straight line. The value 10 is the height, not the missing coordinate. The intercept on the \(y\)-axis, where \(x = 0\), would be 10. Half of 10 is 5, which forgets the coefficient 2.

questions.prompt: One of these steps is false. Select that step, and the reason it fails. The function is \(f(x, y) = x^2 + y^2\).
questions.explanation: The origin really does have value 0. The last step only applies the definition stated above it, and that definition is the contour set, not the sublevel set. The sublevel set at height 4 is \(x^2 + y^2 \le 4\), which contains the origin. The contour is the circle of radius 2. The origin is a minimum, not a maximum, and the squares are allowed to be added.
questions.figure: <svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 300 230" role="img" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.6" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="12"><title>nested ellipses</title><line x1="28" y1="118" x2="272" y2="118"/><polygon points="272,118 265.6,120.7 265.6,115.3" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><line x1="150" y1="204" x2="150" y2="26"/><polygon points="150,26 152.7,32.4 147.3,32.4" fill="currentColor" stroke="none"/><text x="266" y="134" text-anchor="end" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">x1</text><text x="158" y="30" text-anchor="start" font-size="11" fill="currentColor" stroke="none">x2</text><ellipse cx="150" cy="118" rx="40" ry="24"/><ellipse cx="150" cy="118" rx="72" ry="44"/><ellipse cx="150" cy="118" rx="104" ry="62"/></svg>
questions.figure_alt: Three nested ellipses centered at the origin.
steps: The origin has value 0, which is not equal to 4.
A sublevel set keeps only the points where the function equals the height.
Applying that definition to the origin excludes it, because its value is not 4.
reasons: The sublevel set keeps every point whose value is at most 4, so the origin belongs to it.
The origin is a maximum of this function, so every sublevel set excludes it.
Squared coordinates cannot be added, so the value at the origin is not 0.

questions.prompt: When a planar optimization problem is solved by drawing, the objective is shown as
questions.explanation: The drawing overlays contours of the objective on the feasible set and looks for the contour of best height that still touches the feasible set. A vertex is a candidate point, not the picture of the objective. A constraint normal describes the boundary of the feasible set. The empty set would mean there is nothing to draw. Contours are the picture a graphical solve actually uses.

questions.prompt: The sublevel set of \(f(x, y) = x^2 + 4 y^2\) at height 36 meets the positive \(y\)-axis in a segment. What is the largest \(y\)-coordinate on that segment?
questions.explanation: On the positive \(y\)-axis, \(x = 0\) and the sublevel inequality is \(4 y^2 \le 36\), so \(y^2 \le 9\) and \(0 \le y \le 3\). The largest coordinate is 3. The equality \(4 y^2 = 36\) describes the contour, which meets the ray at that same endpoint and nowhere else. The positive \(x\)-intercept of the contour solves \(x^2 = 36\) and equals 6. The height 36 is not the coordinate. The filled sublevel set is closed and bounded, which is the compactness a later existence argument uses.

questions.prompt: The contour set of \(f(x, y) = 3x - y\) at one fixed height is
questions.explanation: An equality \(3x - y = a\) is one linear equation, hence a line. It is not a disk or an ellipse, because those come from quadratic equations. A single height does not collapse the line to a point. The sublevel set at the same height is a closed half-plane, which is what a linear constraint looks like in a graphical linear program.
